current_repo_note: One repository that changed hands within eight months: it began under ComposioHQ, passed through a personal account and Untrivial-ai, and now sits under the OrchestratorInc organisation; the same repository id resolves under all four names, and the README's own links still use the Untrivial-ai name. The hosted cloud web app is a private submodule that is not in the public tree.
canonical_data: sessions, worktrees, pull request and check state, conversations, worker status reports, scheduled automations and their runs, and review runs in a local SQLite database, plus per-session git worktrees on the host
strengths: Supervision is closed-loop and lives in AO's own code: an observer watches pull requests, CI and review threads, a lifecycle manager decides what is actionable, and the message goes back to the session that owns the branch, with the last nudge signature persisted to avoid repeats
A persistent orchestrator session is separate from worker sessions in the schema, and workers report checkpoint, needs-input, stuck or done through a delivery outbox with acknowledgement
Adapters cover about forty harnesses and several ACP chat drivers, and the scheduler stores recurrence rules with leased, retried runs
weaknesses: The root licence is Apache-2.0 and was only added on 2026-06-27, while the frontend and command-line packages declare MIT in their manifests without a licence file of their own
No spend cap or budget policy was found; usage is tracked but nothing enforces a limit
The hosted web app is a private submodule, the terms URL under the new domain returned 404, and the README says the renderer sends anonymous usage events to PostHog
Eight months of history show 188 numbered schema migrations, repeated renumbering fixes, and four owner names, so card claims will drift quickly
why_it_matters: The most developed answer yet to the question of who keeps a fleet of pull requests moving: an orchestrator that watches CI and review state itself and pushes the feedback back to the agent that owns it.
